What you received

Extract the ZIP to an ordinary folder and open index.html directly. Local search, asset tables and progress controls do not require a web server. Internet is needed only for external reference links, installing tools and the online game you will later implement.

The supplied art ZIP was not accessible in this task. Phase00 must acquire the privately licensed archive and run its audit before exact slicing or plugin-specific art setup is considered ready. Legal debug sprites can de-risk movement; they do not satisfy the source-art acceptance gate.

Use the manual in this order

  1. Read architecture.html and architecture/source-migration.html to understand why the old local-save platformer model is replaced.
  2. Open sources-verification.html and distinguish public documentation checked from installed API compatibility not checked.
  3. Read Phase00, create only its asset order, then follow each asset technical page. Use the Content/Source paths exactly.
  4. After native build, create the current Blueprint children and Data Assets; assign them into existing consumers listed under phase integration.
  5. Edit the named map, run its fixture, then record success, rejection and previous-phase regression. Do not mark a phase done just because its assets exist.
  6. Use first-vertical-slice.html for three acceptance routes. Character creation/persistence/travel grow before combat; professions/social/content expansion follow the working foundation.

First-time terminology

An Actor is an object placed or spawned in a world. A Pawn is an Actor that can be controlled; Character adds capsule-oriented movement. PlayerController handles a player connection/input, PlayerState carries replicated in-zone player facts, GameState broadcasts shared world facts, GameMode contains server-only world rules, and GameInstance exists once per process. None of these engine lifetimes is a database.

A Blueprint is an Editor-authored class or visual graph. A Data Asset is read-only authored configuration. C++ owns validation and mutation; Blueprint children expose tuning and visual assignments. A compiled class and a described class are different things.

A dedicated server has no local player viewport. Two PIE windows are useful but do not prove remote deployment. An RPC asks another network machine to execute a function under engine ownership rules; a server RPC is not a general function anyone may invoke on any world Actor. Replication sends approved state, not every member variable automatically.

Prepare an implementation workspace

  1. Install the actual Unreal5.8.3 source/toolchain route required by the chosen dedicated-server build; record engine changelist, compiler, SDK and platform. No installation was inspected here.
  2. In Unreal create a Blank C++ desktop project named RPG with starter content optional. Keep the game implementation repository separate from this documentation repository.
  3. Enable Paper2D and Enhanced Input, restart when prompted. Add Gameplay Ability System dependencies at Phase07. Obtain PaperZD from its legitimate provider and verify descriptor/source support before choosing exact animation factories.
  4. Create Content/Game domain folders only as current assets need them. Add the RPG native module folders from engineering/naming-and-content.html.
  5. Create L_TerrainLab with a floor and clear PlayerStart, BP_ZoneGameMode and BP_PlayerCharacter/BP_RPGPlayerController. Build native classes before Blueprint parent selection.
  6. Make a normal source-control commit after each accepted phase. Store secrets, licensed source archives and generated engine intermediates outside public documentation.

Do not confuse three milestones

Reading/checking these docs is a documentation milestone. Creating and compiling classes is an implementation milestone. Running two remote clients against the backend and server is a gameplay acceptance milestone. Record evidence independently; this edition has no engine compile or runtime evidence.
